title_zh: 奥司他韦基有机盐和离子液体:理化性质、细胞毒性和神经氨酸酶抑制
source_body_en: Background: Neuraminidase (NA) inhibitors are widely used for the treatment of influenza, but the emergence of resistance and limitations in drug formulation can compromise their therapeutic performance. This study investigated whether counterion exchange can modulate the physicochemical properties, cytotoxicity, and NA-inhibitory activity of oseltamivir (OS) while preserving its covalent structure. Methods: Five OS-based ionic formulations, [OS][C1SO3], [OS][C3SO3], [OS][C6SO3], [OS][TolSO3], and [OS][CSA], were synthesized and characterized by NMR and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, with isolated yields ranging from 84 to 88%. Spectroscopic data confirmed the formation of the desired 1:1 salts and showed that the OS ethyl ester remained chemically intact. The formulations were evaluated for aqueous solubility, octanol/water partitioning, cytotoxicity toward MDCK-SIAT1 cells, and NA-inhibitory activity using a MUNANA-based assay against NAs from A(H1N1)pdm09, its H275Y oseltamivir-resistant variant, A(H3N2), and type B influenza viruses. Results: All formulations exhibited low cytotoxicity, with CC50 values above 1200 μM. All OS ionic formulations showed lower IC50 values than oseltamivir phosphate against all four influenza viruses, with improvements ranging from approximately 2.5- to 393-fold. [OS][TolSO3] showed the highest potency, reducing the IC50 by approximately 336-fold against H275Y virus NA and 393-fold against influenza B virus NA. IC90 values showed the same overall potency ranking, although improvements at 50% inhibition were not always proportionally maintained at 90% inhibition. Conclusions: Overall, counterion selection substantially influenced both the physicochemical and biological profiles of OS. [OS][TolSO3] provided the highest NA-inhibitory potency, whereas [OS][CSA] exhibited the most balanced overall profile, supporting counterion engineering as a potential approach to optimize oseltamivir-based ionic formulations.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 神经氨酸酶 (NA) 抑制剂广泛用于流感 治疗,但耐药性的出现和药物配方的限制可能会影响其治疗效果。本研究调查了抗衡离子交换是否可以调节奥司他韦 (OS) 的理化性质、细胞毒性和 NA 抑制活性,同时保留其共价结构。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及使用 NMR 和 ATR-FTIR 光谱合成和表征五种基于 OS 的离子制剂:[OS][C1SO3]、[OS][C3SO3]、[OS][C6SO3]、[OS][TolSO3] 和 [OS][CSA]。评估了制剂的水溶性、辛醇/水分配、对 MDCK-SIAT1 细胞的细胞毒性,以及对来自 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、其 H275Y 奥司他韦抗性变体、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B 型流感病毒的 NA 的 NA 抑制活性。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些制剂通过核磁共振和ATR-FTIR光谱法进行了合成和表征,其单独产率范围为84到88%。
analysis_zh.main_results: 光谱数据证实了所需 1:1 盐的形成,并表明 OS 乙酯在化学上保持完整。所有制剂均表现出低细胞毒性,CC50 值高于 1200 μM。所有 OS 离子制剂对所有四种流感病毒的 IC50 值均低于磷酸奥司他韦,改善范围约为 2.5 至 393 倍。[OS][TolSO3] 显示出最高的效力,针对 H275Y 病毒 NA 的 IC50 降低了约 336 倍,针对乙型流感病毒 NA 的 IC50 降低了 393 倍。IC90 值显示出相同的总体效力排名,尽管 50% 抑制时的改善并不总是按比例维持在 90% 抑制时。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体而言,抗衡离子的选择极大地影响了 OS 的物理化学和生物学特征。[OS][TolSO3] 提供最高的 NA 抑制效力,而 [OS][CSA] 表现出最平衡的整体特征,支持反离子工程作为优化基于奥司他韦的离子制剂的潜在方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,抗衡离子工程可能是一种有前景的策略,可增强基于奥司他韦的离子制剂对 季节性流感 病毒 治疗 的治疗潜力,特别是在解决耐药性和提高药物溶解度和活性方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外评估,不包括体内或临床数据。证据是中等的,因为结果基于实验室实验,没有考虑现实世界的变异性或长期影响。

title: Co-circulation of H5N1 and H5N6 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in migratory birds at a coastal wintering site in China.
abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. In this study, we report the co-circulation of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and H5N6 HPAIVs associated with mortality events in Anseriformes and Charadriiformes at a coastal wintering site in Fujian Province, China. H5N1 and H5N6 viruses were identified in four species of waterfowl (Bean Goose, Eastern Spot-billed Duck, Eurasian Wigeon, and Eurasian Curlew). Phylogenetic analysis indicated that these H5N1 and H5N6 isolates were clade 2.3.4.4b strains circulating within Eurasia and lacked known mammalian adaptation markers in key proteins. The infected birds exhibited severe systemic multi-organ pathology, with the most pronounced damage observed in the lungs. H5N6 and H5N1 viruses caused lethal injury in BALB/c mice, with H5N1 leading to systemic infection. Environmental sampling also revealed the presence of H5N1 HPAIVs alongside low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) such as H3N1 and H6N1. Our findings highlight the complex and dynamic transmission patterns of H5 HPAIV in wild bird populations and the substantial threat they pose to mammals, underscoring the critical importance of sustained surveillance for high pathogenicity avian influenza in wild birds.

title: Variable transmission efficiency of mammalian origin HPAI D1.1 H5N1 strains in ferrets
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 lineage continues to predominate in the United States wild bird population and has spilled over into dairy cattle three independent times. To assess the transmission risk of this sublineage, we performed direct-contact transmission experiments for three distinct D1.1 strains in ferrets. Two of these strains were isolated from humans and one from a lethal cat infection. We found that only one human isolate (A/NV/10/2025) was able to transmit efficiently between ferrets. Compared to the other strains, this isolate harbored the mammalian adaptive PB2 D701N mutation, suggesting this mutation may be a candidate contributing to enhanced transmission efficiency of D1.1 as opposed to the PB2 E627 K substitution present in the lethal cat isolate. Based on these data we conclude that the transmission fitness of D1.1 strains is modest but special attention should be paid to emergence of adaptation at the PB2 701 position.

title: INFLUENZA SAZONAL: DIAGNÓSTICO, VIGILÂNCIA E PREVENÇÃO NA MEDICINA — UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA
abstract: Introdução: A influenza sazonal é uma infecção respiratória aguda de circulação anual, responsável por elevada carga de hospitalizações, óbitos e custos aos sistemas de saúde. Objetivo: Sintetizar as evidências científicas publicadas entre 2021 e 2026 sobre diagnóstico, vigilância epidemiológica e prevenção da influenza sazonal. Metodologia: Revisão sistemática conduzida conforme as recomendações PRISMA 2020, com busca na base PubMed/MEDLINE por meio de estratégia booleana combinando descritores MeSH e termos livres relacionados à influenza humana, sazonalidade, diagnóstico, vigilância e vacinação. Dos 4.922 registros identificados, 70 estudos publicados entre 2021 e 2026 foram incluídos. Resultados: Os estudos foram agrupados em cinco eixos: aspectos clínicos e diagnósticos; vigilância epidemiológica, genômica e modelagem preditiva; efetividade e recomendações vacinais; novas plataformas vacinais, com destaque para as vacinas de RNA mensageiro; e cobertura vacinal, hesitação e grupos prioritários. A vacinação anual permanece como principal estratégia preventiva, embora sua efetividade varie conforme a temporada, o subtipo viral circulante e a faixa etária. A pandemia de COVID-19 alterou a dinâmica de circulação da influenza, incluindo o provável desaparecimento da linhagem B/Yamagata. Conclusão: O controle da influenza sazonal depende da integração entre diagnóstico laboratorial oportuno, vigilância sentinela e genômica contínua, vacinação anual com ampla cobertura e enfrentamento da hesitação vacinal, especialmente em gestantes, idosos, crianças e imunocomprometidos.

abstract_zh: 简介: 流感是一种由呼吸道感染引起的每年循环的流感,可响应医院的紧急运输、系统和客户的要求。目标:作为 2021 年和 2026 年公共科学证据的科学诊断、流行病学警戒和流感区域预防。方法:修订 PRISMA 2020 推荐系统,以 PubMed/MEDLINE 为基础,结合 MeSH 和人类流感相关术语、诊断、诊断和警戒疫苗接种。包括 4.922 项注册登记、2021 年和 2026 年期间的 70 项公共研究。结果: 第五次研究中的孔洞研究:临床和诊断方面;流行病学、基因组和预测模型的警戒;有效和推荐疫苗;Novas vacinais 平台,com destaque para as vacinas de RNA mensageiro;疫苗接种、犹豫和优先事项。每年一次的永久性疫苗接种主要是预防性的,根据不同的情况采取不同的有效措施,以防止病毒循环和预防。COVID-19 的大流行改变了流感循环的动态,包括 B/Yamagata 地区的流行病。结论:流感的控制取决于实验室诊断的综合时机、警戒和持续的基因检测、每年的疫苗接种和疫苗接种的犹豫,特别是妊娠期、妊娠期和新生儿期的疫苗接种。免疫受损。

title: Host miR-140-5p Directly Targets IFIT2 and Enhances Replication of a Zoonotic Reassortant Swine H3N2 Influenza Virus
abstract: Reassortment between the 2009 pandemic H1N1 virus (pdm/09) and endemic swine influenza viruses has generated zoonotic viruses, including A/Swine/Guangxi/NS2783/2010 (H3N2; SW2783). How host microRNAs shape the outcome of such transmission remains poorly defined. We combined iTRAQ-based quantitative proteomics of A549 cells infected with SW2783, the classical swine H1N1 virus SW3861, or the pdm/09 strain CA09 with our previous miRNA-mRNA dataset. Among 2398 proteins consistently quantified, an integrative analysis identified 118 candidate proteins (49, downregulated and 69 upregulated), of which eight, including PPIA and IFIT2, were prioritized as potential virus-response factors. Western blotting showed that RPS29, HMGA2, IFIT2, and PPIA were specifically upregulated in SW2783-infected cells. miR-140-5p reduced nPPIA and IFIT2 protein levels, and dual-luciferase assays supported direct regulation of the IFIT2 3′ UTR, whereas PPIA appeared to be regulated indirectly. Overexpression of miR-140-5p increased SW2783 M-gene transcripts, HA titers, and TCID50 values (p < 0.01) but did not affect replication of SW3861 or CA09. Together, these findings suggest that miR-140-5p promotes replication of the zoonotic reassortant swine H3N2 virus SW2783, at least in part through direct suppression of IFIT2, while its effect on PPIA appears to be indirect. These results identify the miR-140-5p/IFIT2 axis as a potential host regulatory pathway associated with replication of reassortant swine influenza viruses and warrant further investigation of its relevance to zoonotic risk.

title: Genetic ancestry shapes context-dependent immune regulation across Indigenous South American populations
abstract: Human immune responses remain poorly characterized across Indigenous South American (ISA) populations, limiting our understanding of human immune variation. Here, we generated a single-cell transcriptional atlas of 1.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 345 individuals representing 13 South American populations, profiled at baseline and following stimulation with lipopolysaccharide, influenza A virus, or Trypanosoma cruzi. Genetic ancestry was associated with the expression of a large fraction of the transcriptome, often only after stimulation, and explained more variation than age or sex. On average, cis-eQTLs accounted for one-quarter of these ancestry-associated differences. Thousands of regulatory variants were common in ISA populations but rare or absent in European reference datasets. Integrating eQTLs with GWAS revealed stimulation-specific disease-associated regulatory variants and an enrichment of ancestry-associated expression differences among genes with colocalizing signals. Our findings highlight the importance of studying diverse populations across immune contexts to understand the genetic architecture of human immune responses.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to understand immune variation across Indigenous South American populations by generating a single-cell transcriptional atlas of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 345 individuals. The research found that genetic ancestry significantly influenced immune responses, particularly after stimulation with influenza A virus, and that cis-eQTLs explained a quarter of these ancestry-related differences. The study also identified thousands of regulatory variants common in Indigenous populations but rare in European datasets. These findings emphasize the need to study diverse populations to uncover the genetic basis of immune responses. However, the study's results are limited to the context of immune stimulation and do not provide direct insights into seasonal influenza viruses. The evidence is strong, but the interpretation is grounded in the observed data without extending to causal conclusions.

title: Intratumoral influenza A virus infection drives platinum resistance and invasive reprogramming in NSCLC
abstract: Respiratory viral infections are frequent in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet whether intratumoral viral presence directly influences tumor behavior and therapeutic response remains unknown. Here, we identify a respiratory virus-associated drug metabolism program (REVIS-DM), predominantly expressed by tumor cells and linked to poor clinical outcome. Across multiple NSCLC cohorts, a subgroup of tumors with concurrent high REVIS-DM, interferon-stimulated gene and antiviral signatures was associated with reduced survival and increased relapse after chemotherapy. Consistent with this antiviral profile, Influenza A virus (IAV) transcripts were detected in NSCLC and associated with poor outcome and relapse. Mechanistically, IAV infection induced xenobiotic detoxification, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, invasion, and platinum resistance in vitro and in vivo. These effects required viral sensing and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling but were independent of type I/III interferon pathways. Together, our findings establish intratumoral IAV infection as a previously unrecognized driver of tumor-cell plasticity and chemoresistance in NSCLC, revealing virus-induced metabolic vulnerabilities with potential therapeutic relevance.

The tumor microenvironment (TME) is a critical determinant of NSCLC progression and therapeutic response 4,5. Beyond its immune composition, accumulating evidence indicates that microorganisms shape the TME and influence cancer evolution. The gut microbiota modulates responses to immunotherapy, while intratumoral lung microbiota contributes to tumor progression 6,7. Epidemiological studies further suggest that recurrent respiratory viral infections, particularly with influenza virus, increase lung cancer risk through chronic inflammation and tissue remodeling 8. In other hand, in NSCLC patients, these infections are frequent comorbidities associated with more severe disease course and viral persistence 9–11. H1975, H1650, and HCC827 cells were kindly provided by S. Mouillet-Richard (Centre de Recherche des Cordeliers, Paris, France). Cells were cultured at 37°C under 5% CO2 in DMEM/F12 (Gibco, 11320033) supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated FBS (Eurobio, CVFSVF00), 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin (Gibco, 15140122), 1% L-glutamine (Gibco, 25030081), 1% Non- Essential Amino-Acid (Gibco, 11140050), 1% sodium pyruvate (Gibco, 11360070), and 1% HEPES (Gibco, 15630080). Cisplatin-resistant A549 cells, generated by long-term culture in the presence of increasing concentrations of cisplatin, were kindly provided by G. Kroemer’s laboratory (Centre de Recherche des Cordeliers, Paris, France). Murine KP lung adenocarcinoma cells derived from KrasLSL-G12D/+Trp53flox/flox tumors were kindly provided by L Menger (Institut Gustave Roussy, Paris, France). KP cells were cultured in RPMI 1640 Glutamax (Gibco, 61870036) supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 1% HEPES. Cells were used for fewer than 15 passages. All cell lines were routinely tested for mycoplasma contamination (Ozyme, MORV0011). Cell lines were not authenticated. Influenza A Virus Strains Influenza A virus (IAV) strains A/Scotland/20/74 (H3N2) and A/PR/8/34 (H1N1) were provided by J.M. Sallenave (INSERM UMR 1152, Universite Paris Cite, Paris, France). Viruses were propagated in MDCK cells and purified from culture supernatants by sucrose gradient centrifugation. 7 Reagents Cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin, vinorelbine, paclitaxel, fluorouracil, and gemcitabine were obtained from the pharmacy of Cochin hospital (Paris, France). In vitro IAV Infection For 2D cultures, A549 cells (1.5 x 105 cells/well) were infected with IAV (MOI = 1) for 2 h, washed, and cultured for the indicated times. For 3D cultures, cells were infected in suspension (1 × 105 cells/mL, MOI = 0.1) for 2 h, washed, and seeded in ultra-low attachment 96-well plates (200 cells/well) for 2-3 days. RNA Extraction and RT-qPCR RNA was extracted from cell lysates using NucleoSpin RNA plus or NucleoSpin RNA plus XS kits (Macherey-Nagel, 740984, 740990). RNA from FFPE human tumor samples was isolated using the Maxwell 16 FFPE tissue LEV Purification kit (Promega, AS1260). RNA quality and concentration were assessed using an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer. cDNA synthesis was performed using the high-capacity cDNA reverse transcription kit (Applied Biosystem, 4374966). cDNA concentration was measured using the Qubit ssDNA Assay kit (Invitrogen, Q10212). Quantitative PCR was performed using TaqMan universal master mix II (Applied Biosystems, 4440040) and TaqMan probes listed in Supplementary Table 1. Gene expression was normalized to HPRT1, and relative expression was calculated using the ΔΔCq method. Fold-change was determined by the formula: FC=2-ΔΔCq. Multiplex Gene Expression Profiling Multiplex gene expression analyses were performed using the QuantiGene Plex Gene Expression Assay (Invitrogen). Two custom panels were designed containing genes related to antiviral responses, drug detoxification, EMT, and invasion (Supplementary Tables 2,3). 8 Plates were analyzed on a Luminex FlexMap3D system. Data were normalized using housekeeping genes with Quantigene Plex software. Flow Cytometry Cells were harvested 24 h after IAV infection, washed with PBS containing 10% FBS and incubated with anti-mouse CD16/CD32 antibody (1:50; BD Pharmingen, 553142) to block Fc receptors. Cells were then stained with anti-IAV nucleoprotein (NP-FITC) antibody (Invitrogen, clone MA1-7322) following fixation and permeabilization (eBioscience, 88-8824- 00). Dead cells were excluded using Live/Dead Aqua staining (Invitrogen, L34965). Samples were acquired on a BD LSRFortessa X-20 flow cytometer (BD Biosciences) and analyzed using FlowJosoftware v10 (BD Biosciences). In vitro Chemoresistance Assays Cells (5 x 103/well) were seeded in 96-well plates and infected with IAV (MOI = 1) for 2 h. Cells were washed and treated with chemotherapeutic agents at various concentrations either immediately or 24 h postinfection. Cell viability and cytotoxicity were assessed after 48-72 h using XTT (CyQuant XTT, Invitrogen, X12223) and LDH assays (CyQuant LDH, Invitrogen, C20300), respectively. Absorbance was measured using an Infinite 200 pro microplate reader (Tecan). For fluorescence-based cell counting, cells were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde during 15 min, stained with Hoechst 33342 (NucBlue, Invitrogen, R37605), and imaged using an Operetta CLS high-content imaging system. Cell viability was normalized to untreated controls. siRNA-Mediated Gene Silencing Cells were transfected with siRNAs (FlexiTube, Qiagen) targeting MYD88, MAVS, STAT1, or IL28RA using Lipofectamine RNAiMAX (Invitrogen, 13778150) at a final concentration of 10 μM. After 24 h, cells were cultured in fresh medium for an additional 24 h before IAV infection 9 (H3N2, MOI = 1). After 2 h of incubation, cells were washed to remove unbound viral particles. RNA was collected 24 h post-infection for RT-qPCR analysis. For chemoresistance assays, cells were treated with cisplatin (20 μM) and viability was assessed after 72 h using XTT assays. Single- cell clones were obtained by limiting dilution. Functional IFNAR1 knockout was validated by IFN-β stimulation (100 ng/mL, 18 h) followed by ISG15 quantification. Images were analyzed using ImageJ. Differentially expressed genes were identified using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Fold-changes were obtained from log-transformed expression values as differences in median expression between groups. These cohorts included patients treated with perioperative chemotherapy (neo-adjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy in the Onco-HEGP cohort and neoadjuvant chemotherapy in the Onco-Cochin cohort). Differentially expressed genes were identified using the package DESeq2 and normalized gene expression matrices were obtained using the VST method. Associated 11 clinical annotations were obtained from the corresponding studies. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of intratumoral influenza A virus (IAV) infection on non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progression and therapeutic response. The research identifies a respiratory virus-associated drug metabolism program (REVIS-DM) linked to poor clinical outcomes in NSCLC. Analysis across multiple cohorts reveals that tumors with high REVIS-DM, interferon-stimulated gene, and antiviral signatures show reduced survival and increased relapse after chemotherapy. IAV transcripts were detected in NSCLC and correlated with adverse outcomes. Mechanistically, IAV infection was shown to induce xenobiotic detoxification, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, invasion, and platinum resistance in both in vitro and in vivo models. These effects depend on viral sensing and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling but are independent of type I/III interferon pathways. The findings highlight IAV as a previously unrecognized driver of tumor-cell plasticity and chemoresistance, suggesting potential therapeutic targets related to virus-induced metabolic vulnerabilities.

title_zh: 肿瘤内甲型流感病毒感染驱动非小细胞肺癌的铂类耐药和侵入性重编程
source_body_en: Respiratory viral infections are frequent in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet whether intratumoral viral presence directly influences tumor behavior and therapeutic response remains unknown. Here, we identify a respiratory virus-associated drug metabolism program (REVIS-DM), predominantly expressed by tumor cells and linked to poor clinical outcome. Across multiple NSCLC cohorts, a subgroup of tumors with concurrent high REVIS-DM, interferon-stimulated gene and antiviral signatures was associated with reduced survival and increased relapse after chemotherapy. Consistent with this antiviral profile, Influenza A virus (IAV) transcripts were detected in NSCLC and associated with poor outcome and relapse. Mechanistically, IAV infection induced xenobiotic detoxification, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, invasion, and platinum resistance in vitro and in vivo. These effects required viral sensing and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling but were independent of type I/III interferon pathways. Together, our findings establish intratumoral IAV infection as a previously unrecognized driver of tumor-cell plasticity and chemoresistance in NSCLC, revealing virus-induced metabolic vulnerabilities with potential therapeutic relevance.
abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染在非小细胞肺癌(NSCLC)患者中很常见,但瘤内病毒的存在是否直接影响肿瘤行为和治疗反应仍不清楚。在这里,我们确定了一种呼吸道病毒相关药物代谢程序(REVIS-DM),该程序主要由肿瘤细胞表达,并与不良的临床结果相关。在多种 NSCLC 队列研究 中,同时存在高 REVIS-DM、干扰素刺激基因和 抗病毒药物 特征的肿瘤亚组与化疗后生存率降低和复发增加相关。与此 抗病毒药物 概况一致,在 NSCLC 中检测到甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 转录物,并与不良预后和复发相关。从机制上讲,IAV感染在体外和体内诱导异生物质解毒、上皮间质转化、侵袭和铂耐药。这些效应需要病毒传感和 NLRP3 炎性体信号传导,但独立于 I/III 型干扰素途径。总之,我们的研究结果表明,肿瘤内 IAV 感染是 NSCLC 肿瘤细胞可塑性和化疗耐药性的一个先前未被认识的驱动因素,揭示了病毒诱导的代谢脆弱性,具有潜在的治疗相关性。

full_text: Abstract Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) poses a serious threat to the global poultry industry, causing substantial economic losses while representing a significant challenge to public health and environmental hygiene [1,2]. The objective of this study was to develop a novel non-chemical water treatment technology by combining a unique Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF), generated by opposing like-pole (N–N/S–S) permanent magnets, with naturally strongly acidic hot spring water, and to evaluate its physicochemical characteristics together with its virus- and pathogen-inactivating efficacy [S1-S4]. Physicochemical changes in the treated water before and after Hatano-RCMF exposure were investigated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis [S1,S2]. Biological evaluations were performed by assessing the inactivation of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) [S1], together with representative pathogenic microorganisms, including Escherichia coli O157 [S2] and Salmonella spp. [S2]. The combined treatment of Hatano-RCMF and naturally strongly acidic hot spring water induced measurable physicochemical changes in the water and demonstrated potent inactivation activity against H5N1 as well as representative pathogenic microorganisms [S1,S2]. These findings suggest that this technology represents a promising non-chemical approach for infectious disease control that may reduce dependence on conventional chemical disinfectants. The proposed system has potential applications not only in the poultry and livestock industries but also in the fields of food safety, public health, and environmental hygiene. Introduction Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) has recently caused serious outbreaks worldwide, severely affecting both the poultry industry and wild bird populations. Consequently, it has become a major concern for public health and global food security1,2. Large numbers of poultry have been culled to prevent disease transmission, resulting in substantial economic and social losses to the poultry industry. These circumstances have highlighted the urgent need for the development of safe, sustainable, and non-chemical sanitation technologies that are compatible with the principles of One Health, integrating human, animal, and environmental health3. Naturally strongly acidic hot spring water has attracted increasing attention as an environmentally friendly sanitation resource because of its inherent antimicrobial and antiviral properties derived from its low-pH environment4. In parallel, previous studies have suggested that magnetic field treatment may alter the physicochemical and hydrodynamic properties of water. However, the underlying mechanisms responsible for these effects remain largely unclear. The Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF) employed in this study is a novel fluid-processing technology that utilizes a unique repulsive-collision spatial magnetic field generated by opposing like-pole permanent magnets (N–N and S–S) [S4]. This magnetic configuration produces a distinctive spatial magnetic field layer that may influence the physicochemical properties of fluids. Over many years, the authors have systematically investigated naturally occurring fluids capable of acting synergistically with Hatano-RCMF. Among the various natural fluids evaluated, naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water was identified as the most suitable candidate for combination with Hatano-RCMF. Based on this finding, we developed a novel fluid-processing system integrating Hatano-RCMF with naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water and subsequently produced a prototype functional water designated Tori-Maru Block [S1,S2,S6]. Tori-Maru Block represents a new sanitation water technology that combines the physicochemical effects of Hatano-RCMF with the intrinsic properties of naturally strongly acidic hot spring water. The system was developed primarily for the control of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) in poultry and livestock production [S1], while also targeting representative pathogenic microorganisms, including Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli O157 [S2]. In the present study, physicochemical changes in the treated water were evaluated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis [S3]. In addition, independent third-party laboratories conducted biological evaluations of antiviral and antimicrobial activities [S1,S2]. Through these complementary physicochemical and biological assessments, we comprehensively investigated the effectiveness and potential applicability of the integrated Hatano-RCMF–naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water system [S1,S2]. This study was designed as an initial evaluation of the overall integrated system. The individual contributions of each component and the detailed mechanisms underlying their synergistic effects will be investigated in future studies using appropriate controlled experimental designs (Fig. 1). In the repulsive magnetic field generated by opposing like poles (N–N/S–S), the magnetic fluxes repel each other at the center of the configuration, causing the magnetic field lines to bend at approximately 90°. Within this collision region, a heterogeneous (mottled) magnetic field structure is formed at the center, while stable longitudinal striped spatial magnetic field layers, each approximately 1 mm in width, develop on both sides of the central region [S4]. In the present study, this characteristic magnetic field configuration is collectively defined as the Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF). Hatano-RCMF represents a unique spatial magnetic field architecture generated by the repulsive interaction between opposing like-pole permanent magnets (N–N/S–S) and constitutes a previously unreported magnetic field environment that is distinct from the conventional attractive magnetic fields produced by opposite-pole (N–S) configurations [S4]. This spatial magnetic field layer is suggested to interact with water, other fluids, biological systems, and microorganisms, thereby potentially inducing a wide range of physicochemical and biological effects5,6,7,8,9. Materials and methods Figure 2 Structural configuration of the experimental water-flow system incorporating the external Hatano-RCMF device. Figure 2 illustrates the configuration of the experimental water-flow system. The external Hatano-RCMF device was mounted around the outside of the pipeline, allowing the fluid to pass continuously through the repulsive-collision magnetic field layer under continuous-flow conditions [S4]. An exploded front view of the Hatano-RCMF device is shown. The left and right units each contain embedded neodymium permanent magnets arranged so that identical poles (N–N or S–S) directly oppose one another [S4]. Upon assembly, the configuration generates the Hatano-RCMF spatial magnetic field layer in the central region between the opposing magnets. An exploded top view of the Hatano-RCMF device is presented. The left and right units are connected and precisely aligned using fixing insertion bars, which maintain a constant separation distance between the opposing magnets. This configuration ensures the stable formation of the N–N/S–S repulsive magnetic field and provides high experimental reproducibility. Description of the fixing insertion bars The fixing insertion bars are mechanical components designed to connect and secure the left and right Hatano-RCMF units. These bars maintain precise alignment and a constant separation distance between the opposing permanent magnets, thereby ensuring stable formation of the Hatano-RCMF spatial magnetic field layer. In addition, the design facilitates convenient assembly, disassembly, and routine maintenance of the device. The Hatano-RCMF device proposed in this study was designed for external installation on the straight section of a water supply pipe downstream of the water meter. Because the device can be mounted without cutting, modifying, or otherwise altering the existing pipeline, it can be readily installed and removed from a wide variety of water supply systems, including residential buildings, commercial facilities, apartment complexes, water storage tanks, and well-water piping. This design provides excellent ease of installation, maintenance, and serviceability, making the system readily applicable to existing water distribution infrastructure. To evaluate its practical applicability, installation tests were conducted using both gunmetal (bronze alloy) piping and rigid polyvinyl chloride (PVC) piping. In both cases, the Hatano-RCMF device was securely mounted and consistently generated a stable Hatano-RCMF spatial magnetic field layer, demonstrating excellent mechanical stability and installation compatibility. Because the proposed system can be introduced without substantial modification of existing infrastructure, it has potential applications in a broad range of settings, including residential and commercial water systems, food-processing facilities, agricultural and poultry production, healthcare and nursing-care facilities, and various industrial piping systems. The externally mounted retrofit design represents one of the principal advantages of the proposed technology, providing high levels of installation flexibility, reproducibility, maintainability, and practical applicability for real-world implementation. Hatano-RCMF device All experiments were performed using a prototype Hatano-RCMF device developed based on the conceptual design illustrated in Fig. 1. The Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF) device used in this study consisted of two neodymium permanent magnets with a surface magnetic flux density of approximately 1.2 T, arranged in an opposing like-pole configuration (N–N or S–S). The outer perimeter of the magnetic assembly was enclosed by a soft iron yoke to stabilize and concentrate the magnetic flux [S4]. Using this configuration, a repulsive magnetic field region was generated in the central space between the opposing like-pole permanent magnets. In the present study, this unique magnetic field region is defined as the Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (RCMF). The prototype device was designed for 20A (nominal 20-mm diameter) water piping and was externally mounted on the outside of the pipeline, allowing the flowing water to be exposed to the magnetic field without direct contact with the device (Fig. 2). Experimental water-flow system The experimental water-flow system was designed as an externally mounted unit intended for practical applications in residential, commercial, and small-scale water supply systems. The device was engineered to allow easy installation and removal without modification of existing pipelines. This design enabled the reproduction of water-flow conditions representative of actual operating environments, as well as laboratory-scale experiments. Municipal tap water was used throughout the study under continuous-flow conditions simulating a typical domestic water supply system. A transparent acrylic pipe with an inner diameter of 20 mm was employed as the flow channel to allow direct visual observation of the water flow during the experiments. The Hatano-RCMF device was externally mounted on the outside of the pipeline, and continuous unidirectional water flow was maintained throughout all experiments. The experimental conditions were as follows: - Water source: Municipal tap water - Flow channel: Transparent acrylic pipe (20 mm inner diameter) - Flow mode: Continuous water flow - Ambient temperature: 22 °C (23 °C in selected experiments) - Laboratory environment: Wind-free conditions under constant illumination Hatano-RCMF device: Two externally mounted Hatano-RCMF units, each consisting of two neodymium permanent magnets (surface magnetic flux density approximately 1.2 T) enclosed within a soft iron yoke. Preparation of Hatano-RCMF functional water For Hatano-RCMF treatment, the direction of water flow, flow rate, and device configuration were standardized to ensure that the fluid consistently passed through the Hatano-RCMF spatial magnetic field layer under identical conditions. This standardized protocol ensured the reproducibility and comparability of all experimental evaluations while allowing the physicochemical effects of the magnetic field treatment to be assessed objectively9. Hatano-RCMF functional water was prepared by continuously passing municipal tap water through two Hatano-RCMF devices connected in parallel, each installed at an inclination angle of approximately 60°, thereby exposing the flowing water to the Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (RCMF) during continuous flow9. All experiments were conducted under identical operating conditions to ensure experimental reproducibility. For the viral and bacterial inactivation studies, naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water (pH approximately 2.1) was processed using the same treatment protocol by passing it continuously through two parallel Hatano-RCMF devices. The resulting treated hot spring water was used as the evaluation sample for subsequent biological assays4. Characteristics of the test sample (Naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water) The naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water used in this study is characterized by its naturally occurring multi-element composition and its ability to maintain a stable acidic pH over prolonged periods. In addition to evaluating these intrinsic properties, the present study compared the performance of the hot spring water with that of municipal tap water to investigate its potential synergistic effects when combined with Hatano-RCMF treatment4. To further characterize the treated water, elemental composition and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analyses were performed. The resulting data were comprehensively evaluated to investigate the relationship between physicochemical changes induced by Hatano-RCMF treatment and the observed hygienic efficacy [S3,S6]. Naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water (pH approximately 2.1) supplied by Nakanosawa Onsen Co., Ltd. was used as the test water throughout this study. The same batch of hot spring water was used consistently for all viral inactivation assays, bacterial inactivation assays, and physicochemical evaluations to ensure experimental consistency. Figure 3 illustrates the preparation process for Hatano-RCMF-treated functional water. Naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water (pH approximately 2.1) was allowed to flow downward under gravity along a pipeline inclined at approximately 60° and was passed through an externally mounted Hatano-RCMF device incorporating opposing like-pole permanent magnets (S–S/N–N configuration). The treated water was subsequently filtered through a 1-μm polypropylene (PP) filter to produce Hatano-RCMF-treated functional water. The Hatano-RCMF device was designed to apply the magnetic field externally through the pipeline wall without requiring any modification of the internal pipe structure. This externally mounted configuration enables straightforward installation on existing water supply and recirculation piping systems, thereby providing a practical platform for large-scale implementation and field applications. The Hatano-RCMF-treated functional water prepared using this procedure was used for comprehensive evaluation, including assays of total viable bacteria, coliform bacteria, Escherichia coli O157, Salmonella spp., highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1), and physicochemical characterization by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy [S1,S2,S3,S6]. A notable advantage of the proposed system is its practicality for poultry biosecurity applications. In poultry farms, the treated functional water can be applied through automated mist spraying two to three times daily or supplied as diluted drinking water. Furthermore, because the Hatano-RCMF device can be retrofitted onto existing piping systems without extensive infrastructure modification, the proposed technology is well suited for practical field implementation and large-scale validation studies (Fig. 4). Chemical composition analysis of Nakanosawa hot spring water The naturally strongly acidic Nakanosawa hot spring water used in this study was identified by Tatsuo Hatano as a promising natural resource because of its exceptionally strong acidity, long-term physicochemical stability, and potential applicability in hygienic and public health fields [S6]. This hot spring is characterized by an exceptionally high discharge rate of approximately 13,400 L min−1 from a single spring outlet, making it one of the largest naturally strongly acidic hot springs in Japan [S6]. This abundant and stable water supply provides a practical foundation for the large-scale production of functional water and its continuous application in poultry and livestock biosecurity. The chemical composition of the hot spring water was independently analyzed by the Chiba Pharmaceutical Association Inspection Center, an accredited third-party analytical laboratory [S6]. The analytical results demonstrated that the hot spring water was primarily composed of sulfate (SO42−) and chloride (Cl−) ions and contained a characteristic chemical composition consisting of 76 elemental and physicochemical constituents, including calcium (Ca), silicon (Si), and sodium (Na) [S6]. These analytical data provide baseline evidence supporting the chemical quality and reproducibility of the natural hot spring water used throughout this study [S6]. To develop a novel functional water, the naturally strongly acidic hot spring water was subsequently treated using the Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF) technology. The Northern Hemisphere flu season is starting weeks ahead of schedule. The very beginning of the epidemic is caused by an H1N1 virus carrying a mutation that worries virologists and epidemiologists. This vaccine prepared for the 2026/2027 season has been rebuilt in all three of its components. Both facts point to the same advice: we should vaccinate earlier than usual, and the shot should not be a simple formality. The season is already running ahead of schedule, with influenza positivity unusually high for early autumn in the United Kingdom and on the United States (US) West Coast. In Japan, the exceptionally early outbreak observed already in August and early September provoked the closure of some schools.1 What is different about the virus? In the week ending September 26, 2026, H1N1 accounted for 96% of subtyped positive cases in the US, H3N2 for almost 4%, and influenza B was not detected, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) surveillance.2 This early-season subtype distribution contrasts with that observed during the previous influenza season, when H3N2 subclade K predominated. Sequencing points to a mutation in H1N1 called G155E. Alex Greninger’s laboratory at the University of Washington found it in 13 of 17 H1N1 samples from Seattle with sufficiently complete sequences. In a preprint from Jesse Bloom’s laboratory,3 antibodies in 260 blood samples from Australia and the US recognized some G155E-bearing strains less well, especially in sera from teenagers and young adults, who have probably not met similar H1N1 viruses before. The preprint has not yet been peer-reviewed. It measured pre-existing antibodies, not those produced by this year’s vaccine. And a handful of Seattle sequences is not a national picture. None of this is a reason for alarm; all of it is a reason for attention and further surveillance. Meanwhile, the vaccine for the 2026/2027 season has been rebuilt in all three components. The World Health Organization recommendation of February 27, 2026,4 replaces every strain. All vaccines carry an A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09-like virus. Egg-based vaccines add A/Darwin/1454/2025 (H3N2) and B/Tokyo/EIS13- 175/2025 (B/Victoria); cell-, recombinant- and nucleic-acid-based vaccines use A/ Darwin/1415/2025 and B/Pennsylvania/14/2025. The European Medicines Agency followed this recommendation.5 The choice was made in February 2026, 7 to 10 months before the season, as the Bloom preprint noted.3 That lead time is the structural weakness of egg- and cell-based manufacture: the virus keeps changing while the vaccine is being made. Whether the Journal of Clinical and Journal of Clinical and Translational Research Translational Research Editorial Volume x Issue x (2026) 2  doi: 10.36922/JCTR026420119 new H1N1 strain covers G155E-bearing viruses well is not something the sources available now settle, and it is too early to claim it. Laboratories will test it in the coming weeks, and agencies should publish those results promptly. None of this changes the case for vaccination. A vaccine that matches only partly still tends to protect better against severe disease than no vaccine, which is the outcome that fills hospital beds. The unusually early start to the season also calls for a second look at vaccination timing. The standard counsel has been to vaccinate in September or October, and to avoid July or August because immunity can wane over the season, especially in people aged 65 and over. CDC interim guidance for 2026–20276 keeps that logic, preferring completion by the end of October while encouraging vaccination for as long as viruses circulate. It is reasonable to consider receiving the influenza vaccine as soon as possible. The reason to delay was a possible loss of protection by February 2027. However, the reason to go now is an epidemic that may peak sooner than usual. Last year, Europe saw influenza detections three to four weeks earlier than in the two previous seasons. This year, it comes even faster. Anyone who has not yet been vaccinated, and above all those aged 65 and over, pregnant women, patients with chronic conditions, and health workers, should do so this month. Someone who got a shot in September need not do anything more, and CDC advises no booster dose for people already fully vaccinated this season. Alongside these timing concerns, new vaccine tools are emerging amid uncertainty surrounding the institutions responsible for vaccine guidance. A newly approved mRNA influenza vaccine is entering the US market for this season. On August 5, the Food and Drug Administration approved Moderna’s mFLUSIVA for adults aged 50–64 and granted accelerated approval for those aged 65 and over.7 It was tested in more than 20,000 adults. The attraction is speed. Whether mRNA shots deliver better protection in everyday use remains to be shown, and only real-world effectiveness data can judge that. The institutions that should help people choose among products are less settled. After the US Department of Health and Human Services replaced the members of the CDC vaccine advisory committee in June 2025, federal court orders halted implementation of that committee’s later votes, and CDC September 1 interim guidance says the July 2025 recommendations remain in effect for 2026–2027.8 The same guidance is silent on mFLUSIVA. Professional societies such as the American Academy of Family Physicians9 and the American Academy of Pediatrics10 have published their own recommendations. That helps, but it leaves clinicians, pharmacists, and patients, especially adults over 65, choosing between high- dose, adjuvanted, recombinant, and now mRNA products with less clarity than a season like this deserves. Against this backdrop, several immediate actions are warranted. The public should get vaccinated this month if eligible and not yet done. We should not wait for a better- matched product, because none is coming before the approaching season peak. Adults aged 65 and over should ask for a high-dose, recombinant, or adjuvanted vaccine where available, as CDC’s guidance prefers. Clinicians and pharmacies should prioritize older adults, pregnant patients, people with chronic conditions, and care staff, and say plainly that the vaccine is to prevent severe disease. Health agencies should publish early-season vaccine effectiveness estimates for H1N1 as soon as the data allow. They should report subtype and G155E frequency openly, so that everyone can follow the season as it unfolds. Regulators and advisory bodies should give clear, timely guidance on newer products such as mFLUSIVA, and restore a functioning, trusted process for national vaccine recommendations. Researchers should test whether antibodies induced by the 2026–2027 vaccines neutralize G155E viruses and share results as preprints within days, not months. The early signals may fade, and the season may prove ordinary. If they do not, the weeks ahead are the ones that count. Conflict of interest Jacek Z. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the early emergence of an H1N1 virus with a G155E mutation, which worries virologists and epidemiologists. The research aims to advise on earlier vaccination due to the unusual early start of the influenza season, with higher positivity rates observed in the UK and US.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involves surveillance of influenza cases in the US, with data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and sequencing data from Jesse Bloom’s laboratory. The study design includes the analysis of H1N1 samples from Seattle and blood samples from Australia and the US.
analysis.methods: Sequencing was performed to identify the G155E mutation in H1N1, and antibody recognition was tested in 260 blood samples from Australia and the US. The study also discusses the composition of the 2026/2027 influenza vaccine.
analysis.main_results: In the week ending September 26, 2026, H1N1 accounted for 96% of subtyped positive cases in the US, with no detection of influenza B. Sequencing points to the G155E mutation in H1N1, and antibodies in some samples recognized some G155E-bearing strains less well.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a reason for attention and further surveillance, noting that the new H1N1 strain may not cover G155E-bearing viruses well. They emphasize the importance of vaccination, even if the vaccine is not fully matched to the circulating strain.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against delaying vaccination, especially for high-risk groups such as those aged 65 and over, pregnant women, and health workers. The study highlights the need for timely vaccination and the importance of new vaccine tools.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges the limitations of egg- and cell-based vaccine manufacturing, which can lag behind changes in the virus. The evidence strength is moderate due to the early stage of the season and the need for further testing of the vaccine against the new strain.

analysis.summary_en: The study highlights the early emergence of an H1N1 virus with a G155E mutation, advising earlier vaccination due to the unusual early start of the influenza season. Sequencing and antibody tests indicate reduced recognition of some G155E-bearing strains, emphasizing the need for timely vaccination and further surveillance.

elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges the limitations of egg- and cell-based vaccine manufacturing, which can lag behind changes in the virus. The evidence strength is moderate due to the early stage of the season and the need for further testing of the vaccine against the new strain.

full_text: Abstract Introduction This study aimed to assess attitudes and vaccination behaviors among primary healthcare workers toward seasonal influenza vaccination and to examine the psychological antecedents underlying their vaccination decisions using the Psychological Antecedents of Vaccination (5C) framework. Materials and Methods This cross-sectional study included 181 healthcare workers employed at primary healthcare institutions affiliated with a provincial health directorate. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to influenza vaccination, together with the seven-point Likert-type 5C scale. Participants who reported having received an influenza vaccine at least once in previous seasons were compared with those who had never been vaccinated. Participants were also compared according to their vaccination status during the 2025-2026 season. Variables showing significant associations in univariable analyses were subsequently entered into a multivariable binary logistic regression model. Results: The participants had a mean age of 38.1 ± 7.2 years, and 75.1% were women. Overall, 33.1% had received an influenza vaccine at least once, whereas only 16.6% had been vaccinated during the 2025-2026 season. Participants who had received an influenza vaccine at least once had higher collective responsibility scores (p = 0.045). Those vaccinated during the current season had lower constraints scores (p = 0.006) and higher calculation scores (p = 0.030). Significant differences across occupational groups were observed in confidence, complacency, constraints, and collective responsibility (p = 0.002, p < 0.001, p = 0.002, and p = 0.022, respectively). In the multivariable analysis, recommending influenza vaccination [adjusted odds ratio (OR): 7.677; 95% confidence interval (CI), 3.024-19.490; p < 0.001], female sex (adjusted OR: 2.852; 95% CI, 1.115-7.296; p = 0.029), and being a physician (adjusted OR: 2.904; 95% CI, 1.160-7.272; p = 0.023) were independently associated with having received an influenza vaccine at least once. Conclusion Influenza vaccination uptake among primary healthcare workers was low, both historically and during the 2025-2026 season. Having recommended influenza vaccination to others, being female, and being a physician were independently associated with previous influenza vaccination, while higher collective responsibility was associated with vaccination history. These findings support the need for multicomponent interventions that address psychological, behavioral, and practical barriers to vaccination while promoting collective responsibility among healthcare workers. Introduction Influenza is a viral disease characterized by acute respiratory tract infection. The virus, which infects millions of people worldwide each year, causes approximately 290,000-650,000 deaths[1]. One in five unvaccinated children and one in ten unvaccinated adults contract seasonal influenza each year[2]. Although the symptoms of the disease can be mild, influenza can cause severe illness and death in high-risk individuals and is associated with high morbidity and mortality in children, older adults, individuals with chronic diseases, and pregnant women[1, 3]. Due to its high transmission rate and pandemic potential, influenza poses a significant public health risk. Seasonal influenza vaccination reduces the occurrence of severe symptoms and hospitalization by providing immunity against the disease[4, 5]. Healthcare workers are at a higher risk of seasonal influenza than other adults[6]. This occupational group, which plays a critical role in the nosocomial transmission cycle because of its close contact with infected patients, may transmit the virus to high-risk patients. Furthermore, significant workforce losses and associated economic burdens occur among healthcare personnel infected with seasonal influenza[7, 8]. Considering these risks, seasonal influenza vaccination for healthcare workers is recommended by authorities in many countries, and in some countries, it is mandatory for employment[9]. A recent survey of 34 European countries found that 33 have an influenza vaccination policy for healthcare personnel, and 16 mandate at least one vaccination for this group, with nine requiring vaccination as a prerequisite for employment[10]. In Türkiye, healthcare workers are among the risk groups for whom the seasonal influenza vaccine is provided free of charge, and vaccination is voluntary[11]. Despite recommendations from health authorities and the free provision of the vaccine, seasonal influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers remains low[12, 13]. In the most recent survey of European Union and European Economic Area countries, healthcare worker vaccination coverage was reported by only nine countries that recommended vaccination and ranged from 16.6% to 62.8%, with a median of 32%[14]. A systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the pooled influenza vaccine uptake among nurses at 44%[15], whereas coverage among healthcare personnel in the United States reached 76.3% in the 2024-2025 season[16]. Vaccine hesitancy is defined as a delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite the availability of vaccination services[17]. In studies examining seasonal influenza vaccine hesitancy among healthcare workers, factors such as doubts about vaccine effectiveness, concerns regarding vaccine safety, and a low perceived personal risk of influenza have emerged as prominent factors[18, 19]. Interventions designed to improve vaccine uptake have produced heterogeneous results, and their effectiveness appears to depend strongly on the behavior-change methods employed[20, 21]. In this context, identifying the underlying causes of vaccine hesitancy among healthcare workers and developing effective strategies to address them are critically important for reducing influenza cases among both healthcare personnel and the general public. The vaccine acceptance process is multidimensional, and the Psychological Antecedents of Vaccination (5C) model was developed by Betsch et al.[22]. The model conceptualizes vaccination decisions across five psychological dimensions: confidence, meaning trust in vaccines and the vaccination system; complacency, meaning a low perceived risk of vaccine-preventable diseases; constraints, meaning practical or psychological barriers to vaccination; calculation, meaning extensive searching for information about the risks and benefits of vaccination; and collective responsibility, meaning the willingness to protect others through one’s own vaccination[22]. This framework provides a comprehensive approach to understanding the psychological factors underlying vaccination decisions and has been shown to explain vaccination behavior better than sociodemographic variables alone[23]. The aim of this study is to determine the factors affecting the attitudes and vaccination behaviors of healthcare workers regarding the seasonal influenza vaccine. Furthermore, this study aimed to investigate the psychological processes underlying participants’ decisions to accept or reject the seasonal influenza vaccine based on the 5C model. Materials and Methods The population of this cross-sectional study consisted of physicians and allied healthcare personnel (midwives, nurses, health officers, medical secretaries, workers, and others) working at primary healthcare institutions affiliated with the İstanbul Provincial Health Directorate. The study aimed to reach the entire population (n = 222). To evaluate the applicability of the questionnaire developed by the researchers, a pilot study was conducted with 15 healthcare workers. The questionnaire, which was finalized after the pilot implementation, was administered using the supervised questionnaire method. This study was approved by İstanbul Medipol University Non-Interventional Clinical Research Ethics Committee (decision number: 1391, date: 13.11.2025). Written informed consent was obtained from all participants before administration. Data were collected over two days, March 2 and 3, 2026, toward the end of the 2025-2026 influenza season, so that vaccination status for that season could be considered essentially complete at the time of data collection. A total of 181 healthcare workers actively working in primary care settings who fully completed the questionnaire were included in the study, corresponding to a response rate of 81.5%. Data Collection Tool The questionnaire, prepared by the researchers based on a literature review, consists of 18 questions divided into three sections and is provided in full, along with an English translation, in Supplementary File 1. Demographic information: This section consists of 10 questions regarding sociodemographic characteristics, such as age, sex, occupation, and educational status. Knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors regarding vaccination: This section included questions aimed at evaluating participants’ knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to vaccination. Vaccination training, influenza vaccine recommendation behavior, frequency of seasonal influenza vaccination, Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination status, and whether the vaccinations of participants’ children and/or first-degree relatives were complete were evaluated. Vaccination in previous seasons was assessed using a single item with three response options (vaccinated regularly every year, vaccinated occasionally but not regularly, or never vaccinated); participants who selected either of the first two options were classified as having been vaccinated at least once. Psychological antecedents of vaccination (5C) scale: The psychological antecedents of vaccination (5C) scale was developed by Betsch et al.[22] based on the World Health Organization’s 3C model[17]. The scale assesses five psychological antecedents that influence vaccination behavior. The confidence subdimension reflects trust in the effectiveness and safety of vaccines, the system that delivers them, and the motivations of policymakers; complacency reflects the perception that vaccine-preventable diseases pose a low risk and that vaccination is therefore unnecessary; constraints refer to perceived structural and psychological barriers that make vaccination difficult; calculation reflects the extent to which individuals engage in extensive information searching about the risks and benefits of vaccination; and collective responsibility reflects the willingness to protect others through one’s own vaccination[22]. Each subdimension consists of three items, and the scale comprises a total of 15 items. The items are rated on a seven-point Likert-type scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree). Therefore, each sub-dimension score ranges from 3 to 21, with higher scores indicating a stronger presence of the respective antecedent. In the original validation study, Cronbach’s alpha coefficients for the subdimensions ranged from 0.71 to 0.85, whereas values ranging from 0.71 to 0.82 were reported in the Turkish validity and reliability study[24]. In the original validation study, higher confidence scores were positively associated with vaccination behavior, whereas higher complacency and constraints scores were negatively associated with vaccination behavior; calculation and collective responsibility were not independent predictors in that sample. The calculation subdimension reflects individuals’ tendency to seek and evaluate information regarding the risks and benefits of vaccines[22]. Statistical Analysis Data analysis was performed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences for Windows (version 27.0; Armonk, NY: IBM Corp., USA). Descriptive statistics are presented as frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations. The normality of numerical variables was assessed using skewness and kurtosis values. Categorical variables were compared using the Pearson chi-square test, and Fisher’s exact test was used when the minimum expected cell count was less than five. Student’s t-test and one-way analysis of variance were used to compare normally distributed numerical variables, and the Bonferroni test was used for post-hoc pairwise comparisons. For comparisons of the 5C subdimensions, professions were categorized into three groups: physicians, midwives/nurses, and other healthcare personnel (health officers, medical secretaries, workers, and others). For the binary logistic regression analysis, professions were dichotomized as physicians and non-physician healthcare workers. Sex, profession, and the behavior of recommending influenza vaccination, all of which were significant in univariable analyses, were entered into the primary multivariable binary logistic regression model using the enter method. Model fit was assessed using the omnibus test of model coefficients, the Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, and the Nagelkerke R2 value. Odds ratios (ORs) were presented with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results A total of 181 of the 222 eligible healthcare workers completed the questionnaire, corresponding to a response rate of 81.5%. The participants had a mean age of 38.1 ± 7.2 years (range, 23-63 years), and 75.1% (n = 136) were women. A university degree or higher was reported by 77.9% (n = 141) of the participants. Of the participants, 17.1% (n = 31) were physicians or specialist physicians, 23.8% (n = 43) were midwives or nurses, and 59.1% (n = 107) belonged to other occupational groups. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups in the remaining four subdimensions. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Introduction This study aimed to assess attitudes and vaccination behaviors among primary healthcare workers toward seasonal influenza vaccination and to examine the psychological antecedents underlying their vaccination decisions using the Psychological Antecedents of Vaccination (5C) framework. Materials and Methods This cross-sectional study included 181 healthcare workers employed at primary healthcare institutions affiliated with a provincial health directorate. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to influenza vaccination, together with the seven-point Likert-type 5C scale. Participants who reported having received an influenza vaccine at least once in previous seasons were compared with those who had never been vaccinated. Participants were also compared according to their vaccination status during the 2025-2026 season. Variables showing significant associations in univariable analyses were subsequently entered into a multivariable binary logistic regression model. Results: The participants had a mean age of 38.1 ± 7.2 years, and 75.1% were women. Overall, 33.1% had received an influenza vaccine at least once, whereas only 16.6% had been vaccinated during the 2025-2026 season. Participants who had received an influenza vaccine at least once had higher collective responsibility scores (p = 0.045). Those vaccinated during the current season had lower constraints scores (p = 0.006) and higher calculation scores (p = 0.030). Significant differences across occupational groups were observed in confidence, complacency, constraints, and collective responsibility (p = 0.002, p < 0.001, p = 0.002, and p = 0.022, respectively). In the multivariable analysis, recommending influenza vaccination [adjusted odds ratio (OR): 7.677; 95% confidence interval (CI), 3.024-19.490; p < 0.001], female sex (adjusted OR: 2.852; 95% CI, 1.115-7.296; p = 0.029), and being a physician (adjusted OR: 2.904; 95% CI, 1.160-7.272; p = 0.023) were independently associated with having received an influenza vaccine at least once. Conclusion Influenza vaccination uptake among primary healthcare workers was low, both historically and during the 2025-2026 season. Having recommended influenza vaccination to others, being female, and being a physician were independently associated with previous influenza vaccination, while higher collective responsibility was associated with vaccination history. These findings support the need for multicomponent interventions that address psychological, behavioral, and practical barriers to vaccination while promoting collective responsibility among healthcare workers. Introduction Influenza is a viral disease characterized by acute respiratory tract infection. The virus, which infects millions of people worldwide each year, causes approximately 290,000-650,000 deaths[1]. One in five unvaccinated children and one in ten unvaccinated adults contract seasonal influenza each year[2]. Although the symptoms of the disease can be mild, influenza can cause severe illness and death in high-risk individuals and is associated with high morbidity and mortality in children, older adults, individuals with chronic diseases, and pregnant women[1, 3]. Due to its high transmission rate and pandemic potential, influenza poses a significant public health risk. Seasonal influenza vaccination reduces the occurrence of severe symptoms and hospitalization by providing immunity against the disease[4, 5]. Healthcare workers are at a higher risk of seasonal influenza than other adults[6]. This occupational group, which plays a critical role in the nosocomial transmission cycle because of its close contact with infected patients, may transmit the virus to high-risk patients. Furthermore, significant workforce losses and associated economic burdens occur among healthcare personnel infected with seasonal influenza[7, 8]. Considering these risks, seasonal influenza vaccination for healthcare workers is recommended by authorities in many countries, and in some countries, it is mandatory for employment[9]. A recent survey of 34 European countries found that 33 have an influenza vaccination policy for healthcare personnel, and 16 mandate at least one vaccination for this group, with nine requiring vaccination as a prerequisite for employment[10]. In Türkiye, healthcare workers are among the risk groups for whom the seasonal influenza vaccine is provided free of charge, and vaccination is voluntary[11]. Despite recommendations from health authorities and the free provision of the vaccine, seasonal influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers remains low[12, 13]. In the most recent survey of European Union and European Economic Area countries, healthcare worker vaccination coverage was reported by only nine countries that recommended vaccination and ranged from 16.6% to 62.8%, with a median of 32%[14]. A systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the pooled influenza vaccine uptake among nurses at 44%[15], whereas coverage among healthcare personnel in the United States reached 76.3% in the 2024-2025 season[16]. Vaccine hesitancy is defined as a delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite the availability of vaccination services[17]. In studies examining seasonal influenza vaccine hesitancy among healthcare workers, factors such as doubts about vaccine effectiveness, concerns regarding vaccine safety, and a low perceived personal risk of influenza have emerged as prominent factors[18, 19]. Interventions designed to improve vaccine uptake have produced heterogeneous results, and their effectiveness appears to depend strongly on the behavior-change methods employed[20, 21]. In this context, identifying the underlying causes of vaccine hesitancy among healthcare workers and developing effective strategies to address them are critically important for reducing influenza cases among both healthcare personnel and the general public. The vaccine acceptance process is multidimensional, and the Psychological Antecedents of Vaccination (5C) model was developed by Betsch et al.[22]. The model conceptualizes vaccination decisions across five psychological dimensions: confidence, meaning trust in vaccines and the vaccination system; complacency, meaning a low perceived risk of vaccine-preventable diseases; constraints, meaning practical or psychological barriers to vaccination; calculation, meaning extensive searching for information about the risks and benefits of vaccination; and collective responsibility, meaning the willingness to protect others through one’s own vaccination[22]. This framework provides a comprehensive approach to understanding the psychological factors underlying vaccination decisions and has been shown to explain vaccination behavior better than sociodemographic variables alone[23]. The aim of this study is to determine the factors affecting the attitudes and vaccination behaviors of healthcare workers regarding the seasonal influenza vaccine. Furthermore, this study aimed to investigate the psychological processes underlying participants’ decisions to accept or reject the seasonal influenza vaccine based on the 5C model. Materials and Methods The population of this cross-sectional study consisted of physicians and allied healthcare personnel (midwives, nurses, health officers, medical secretaries, workers, and others) working at primary healthcare institutions affiliated with the İstanbul Provincial Health Directorate. The study aimed to reach the entire population (n = 222). To evaluate the applicability of the questionnaire developed by the researchers, a pilot study was conducted with 15 healthcare workers. The questionnaire, which was finalized after the pilot implementation, was administered using the supervised questionnaire method. This study was approved by İstanbul Medipol University Non-Interventional Clinical Research Ethics Committee…

title_original: Factors Influencing Influenza Vaccine Acceptance Among Healthcare Workers

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the psychological processes underlying participants’ decisions to accept or reject the seasonal influenza vaccine based on the 5C model. The background highlights that influenza is a viral disease characterized by acute respiratory tract infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 181 healthcare workers actively working in primary care settings who fully completed the questionnaire. The participants had a mean age of 38.1 ± 7.2 years, with 75.1% being women and 17.1% being physicians or specialist physicians.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to influenza vaccination, together with the seven-point Likert-type 5C scale. Variables showing significant associations in univariable analyses were subsequently entered into a multivariable binary logistic regression model. Statistical analysis was performed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences for Windows (version 27.0).
analysis.main_results: Overall, 33.1% of the healthcare workers had received an influenza vaccine at least once, whereas only 16.6% had been vaccinated during the 2025-2026 season. Participants who had received an influenza vaccine at least once had higher collective responsibility scores (p = 0.045). Those vaccinated during the current season had lower constraints scores (p = 0.006) and higher calculation scores (p = 0.030). Significant differences across occupational groups were observed in confidence, complacency, constraints, and collective responsibility (p = 0.002, p < 0.001, p = 0.002, and p = 0.022, respectively).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the uptake of influenza vaccination among healthcare workers was low, both historically and during the 2025-2026 season. They noted that recommending influenza vaccination was independently associated with vaccine acceptance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to improve influenza vaccine acceptance among healthcare workers, particularly by addressing psychological factors such as collective responsibility and constraints. They also highlight the importance of understanding occupational differences in vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which does not allow for causal inferences. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on self-reported data and a single survey, with potential biases related to response rates and participant recall.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the psychological processes influencing influenza vaccine acceptance among healthcare workers using the 5C model. It found that 33.1% of participants had received an influenza vaccine at least once, while only 16.6% were vaccinated during the 2025-2026 season. Significant differences in vaccine acceptance were observed across occupational groups, with physicians and women more likely to be vaccinated. The study highlights the importance of psychological factors such as collective responsibility and constraints in vaccine uptake. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal conclusions, and the evidence is considered moderate due to reliance on self-reported data. The findings suggest potential areas for targeted interventions to improve vaccination rates among healthcare workers.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在基于5C模型调查参与者决定接受或拒绝季节性流感 疫苗的心理过程。背景强调,流感是一种以急性呼吸道感染为特征的病毒性疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项横断面研究针对 181 名在初级保健机构积极工作且完整填写问卷的医护人员进行。参与者的平均年龄为 38.1 ± 7.2 岁,其中 75.1% 为女性,17.1% 为医生或专科医生。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化问卷收集数据,评估与流感 疫苗接种 相关的社会人口特征、知识、态度和行为,以及七点李克特 5C 量表。在单变量分析中显示显着关联的变量随后被输入到多变量二元逻辑回归模型中。使用 Windows 社会科学统计包(版本 27.0)进行统计分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,33.1% 的医护人员至少接种过一次 疫苗 流感疫苗,而在 2025-2026 季节期间只有 16.6% 的人接种过疫苗。至少接受过一次流感 疫苗 的参与者的集体责任感得分较高 (p = 0.045)。在当前季节接种疫苗的人具有较低的约束分数 (p = 0.006) 和较高的计算分数 (p = 0.030)。不同职业群体在自信、自满、约束和集体责任方面存在显着差异(分别为 p = 0.002、p < 0.001、p = 0.002 和 p = 0.022)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,无论是历史上还是 2025-2026 年季节,医护人员对流感 疫苗接种 的吸收率都很低。他们指出,推荐流感 疫苗接种 与 疫苗 接受程度独立相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息,以提高医护人员对流感 疫苗 的接受度,特别是通过解决集体责任和约束等心理因素。他们还强调了了解 疫苗 吸收的职业差异的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,不允许进行因果推断。证据是温和的,因为它基于自我报告的数据和一项调查,存在与响应率和参与者回忆相关的潜在偏差。
